title: Stability Fingerprint Suite and Customer Certification Checklist for Dedicated Throughput
creator: Samira Ortiz
description: Build a repeatable, tenant-aware load testing and benchmarking harness that produces a compact ‘stability fingerprint’ for each Dedicated fleet configuration and provides a prescriptive customer certification checklist. The artifact will be used by Solutions, SRE, and Customer Engineering to validate throughput guarantees and autoscaler behavior before and after customer onboardings and major runtime changes.
background: Customers buying Dedicated want deterministic throughput and predictable degradation characteristics. Existing synthetic suites produce large, noisy results that are hard to compare across fleet versions, tenant mixes, and autoscaling policies. We need a concise, reproducible output (the stability fingerprint) that encodes throughput curves, burst resilience, and tenant-interference sensitivity.
goals:
- Produce a reproducible stability fingerprint JSON and a short human-readable summary for each test run.
- Provide a customer-facing checklist with pass/fail rules for signoff.
- Simulate realistic tenant mixes including small high-QPS tenants, long-context sessions, and cache-hot tenants.
- Validate autoscaler decisions under controlled contention and burst scenarios.
success_metrics:
- Stability fingerprint correlates with production incidents in 90% of historical cases.
- Automated customer certification reduces onboarding time by 30%.
- False-positive failures in acceptance tests under baseline fleets < 5%.
- End-to-end run time for a certification suite <= 90 minutes (configurable).
scope: In scope: harness code, benchmark methodology, customer checklist, dashboards, and CI integration. Out of scope: long-term load lab infra (will reuse existing cluster), billing changes, and SLA contract negotiation.
approach: Create a modular harness composed of: a traffic morphing engine (to transform golden traces into tenancy mixes), a compact scenario DSL (to express burst profiles and long-tail sessions), a stability fingerprint generator (aggregates time-series into a compact fingerprint), and a validator that evaluates fingerprint vs. golden baselines and acceptance rules. Runs will be orchestrated by the existing test-job orchestration layer but produce additional artifacts and visualizations.
harness_components: traffic-morpher: transforms recorded traces/golden templates into multi-tenant QPS schedules
scenario-dsl: declarative profiles for burst, ramp, sustain, and cooldown phases
fingerprint-generator: computes throughput curves, quantile heatmaps, and a compact SHA-like fingerprint
validator: applies customer certification rules and emits pass/fail plus reasons
replayer: optional golden-trace replayer for exact-workload comparisons
reporter: HTML+JSON output packaged for Customer Engineering signoff
benchmark_methodology:
1) Baseline warmup: bring the fleet to steady-state with low background traffic.
2) Burst sweep: incrementally increase synthetic mix of small-tenant bursts to quantify degradation thresholds.
3) Sustained run: run a 30-minute sustain with tenant mix reflecting customer profile to measure throughput slope and cache effectiveness.
4) Interference injection: introduce an adversarial tenant pattern (long-context cache flushes) to test isolation.
5) Autoscaler validation: run controlled overloads to confirm scale-up/down timing and oscillation dampening.
Measurements: report median, p50/p90/p99 latencies, stable throughput window (largest sustained QPS for 95% of window), and a stability score. Use repeated runs (n=5) and report confidence intervals.
customer_acceptance_tests: Certification run: full fingerprint generation and validator pass against customer-specific baseline
Failure-mode confirmation: show that when a known bad config is applied, fingerprint identifies regression and validator fails with clear reason codes
Autoscaler hysteresis: demonstrate scale-up within configured SLO and no unsafe oscillations for 60 minutes
Tenant-mix replay: replay a 24-hour sampled trace at 4x speed and verify no tail-latency regressions beyond threshold
Cold-cache behavior: validate first-10-minute throughput curve matches expectation for heavy-writes workloads
acceptance_criteria: Fingerprint JSON produced and uploaded to artifacts for every run
Validator returns PASS for baseline fleet and FAIL with annotated diffs for regressions
Customer checklist completed with signed artifacts (fingerprint + dashboards) for pilot customer
Run reproducibility: identical DSL + seed produces consistent fingerprints across 3 runs
CI integration: nightly fingerprint sweep runs and alerts on drift > 10% vs golden baseline
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose telemetry for harness runs: per-phase QPS/latency/time-to-scale. Create a Grafana dashboard with 'stability heatmap' and an alert when stability score drops below threshold or when validator fails in CI. Hook alert to #dedicated-certifications channel with run artifact link.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement harness, run against two internal fleet configs, iterate on fingerprint shape. Phase 2 (pilot): run with Customer Engineering and 1 pilot customer, collect feedback and refine validator rules. Phase 3 (GA): add to onboarding playbook and run as part of Dedicated onboarding checklist. Each phase includes a retrospective and an update to onboarding docs.
open_questions: What is the canonical golden baseline for stability fingerprint? (proposal: last GA fleet + synthetic tenant mix)
What thresholds should map to customer-impact severity levels? (need cross-org decision with SRE and Solutions)
How to represent multi-region cross-traffic in a single fingerprint? (currently target single-region runs)
Should validators be strict (fail-fast) or advisory for initial pilots?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic mixes don't reflect real customer behavior -> Mitigation: seed with anonymized production traces
Risk: Long run times slow onboarding -> Mitigation: provide fast-mode quick checks plus deep-mode overnight runs
Risk: Flaky tests due to infra variance -> Mitigation: require >=3 consecutive runs and compare confidence intervals before failing
Risk: Validator rules too brittle -> Mitigation: start advisory, collect pilot data, then tighten rules
